newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Freeport-McMoRan rises.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Freeport-McMoRan rises.

text.p: Shares of Freeport-McMoRan Inc rose sharply before markets opened Monday, boosted by news it was merging with IMC Global Inc.
Heading a pre-open market busy with a spate of merger news, Freeport-McMoRan was trading at 31-1/4, up from a Friday close of 26-8/16.

Freeport-McMoRan, whose assets consist mostly of a 52 percent stake in Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners LP, and IMC announced early Monday they would merge in a stock swap. The deal would leave IMC as the surviving entity.

Among other active stocks, Chips and Technologies Inc rose on news it would be bought by Intel Corp. Shares in the San Jose, Calif., graphics semiconductor maker were trading at 17-3/16, up from a Friday close of 14.
Intel said in a statement early Monday it had entered a definitive agreement to buy Chips and Technologies at a price of $17.50 a share, or about $384 million.

Regency Health Services Inc was trading at 21-3/8, up from a Friday close of 16-6/16. Sun Healthcare Group Inc said Sunday it and Regency had signed an accord under which Sun would buy Regency's shares for $22 each in a deal worth $369 million.

SFX Broadcasting Inc was trading at 61-5/8, up from a close of 61. The Wall Street Journal said Monday a recent rise in the company's shares might be caused by speculation SFX could be takeover target.
Technology stocks also were active before the markets opened.
Dell Computer Corp was trading at 81-1/2 after splitting two for one. The shares closed at 163 Friday.
The personal computer maker is expected to unveil its first personal workstations Monday. Bear Stearns also cut its rating for Dell to attractive from buy.
Cisco Systems Inc was trading at 80 from a close of 79-11/16, and Sun Microsystems Inc was trading at 47, down from its Friday close of 47-2/16.
